title: He skipped every boring part of his life

visible.why: a traffic jam: Spud at the wheel looks at a remote in his hand; Chip beside him tells a joke, hands up
close through the windscreen: Spud lifts the remote, his thumb on the big white fast-forward button
evening at his cottage: Spud walks off with the remote; Chip still sits in the parked car, blinking, his joke cut off
rain: Chip crouches to jump into a big puddle, grinning at Spud; Spud under his umbrella presses the remote
the same street, dry and sunny: Spud alone with his folded umbrella, pleased; no Chip
a long queue at the bakery: Chip balances a bread loaf on his head to make Spud laugh; Spud rolls his eyes and presses the remote
Monday at the office: Chip brings two coffees, smiling; Spud presses the remote without looking up
straight to camera: Spud holds the remote out to us, eyebrows up: would you press it?
an autumn park: middle-aged Spud alone on a bench presses again; far away Chip walks with the other friends
his living room at dusk: middle-aged Spud alone at the window presses once more
a dim living room: Spud at 82 alone on the sofa, the remote dusty on the armrest, the TV dark
close: old Spud finds a small red rewind button on the back of the remote
over his shoulder: on the old TV, Spud and Chip laughing in the car in the traffic jam
his face lit by the TV, laughing with a tear; on the TV the two of them jump into the puddle together
old Spud stands and holds the remote high, pressing the red rewind button
back in the traffic jam at 25: Spud blinks, the remote in his hand; Chip mid-joke beside him
close: Spud lays the remote in the glove box and shuts it
Chip's punchline; Spud bursts into a real belly laugh
the jammed road at sunset; the teal car in the line, the sun at the end of the street
close through the windscreen at sunset: Spud smiles softly, Chip's head on his shoulder
